newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable amid ample liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable amid ample liquidity.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was stable against the dollar in slow early trading on Tuesday, with the market still driven by liquidity issues, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said the rupiah edged lower at the opening following excess rupiah supply, but offshore buying emerged at mid-morning which helped the rupiah rebound.
He said speculation on a band widening seemed to reappear again which kept pressure on the dollar.
One Japanese bank dealer, however, attributed the firming rupiah to some tightening signal in mid-morning.
Overnight money edged up to eight percent from 5.5 percent.
Spot rupiah was at 2,384.5/84.7 at 0310 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,384.5/85.0. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,384.3/84.7 and 2,384.4/84.8, respectively.

The U.S. bank dealer said sentiment on the rupiah remained firm and was expected to continue, aided by offshore interest in the local bond market and the Busang gold project in which Chase Manhattan Corp will syndicate a $1.2 billion loan.
"This money will have to be converted into the rupiah and sustain demand on the rupiah," the dealer said.
Dealers said swap premiums continued to ease on the back of ample rupiah supply, but six-month swaps were stable because of the general election on May 29.
One-month swaps edged down to 11.5/12.5 from 12.00/12.75 on Monday, two to 25.5/26.5 from 26.5/27.5, three to 38.5/39.0 from 38.75/39.00. Six-month were at 78.0/78.5 points.
Bank Indonesia kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,570 and the conversion band at 2,378/2,426 on Monday.
The bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
